groups.title: Oral liquid (A65402ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an adjunctive treatment for asthenia (functional weakness).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 sachet (1 g) at a time, 3 times a day, diluted in water. Children aged 6 years and over: take 1 sachet (1 g) at a time, 2 times a day, diluted in water. Do not use this medicine for more than 4 weeks.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is an infant under 6 years of age, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breast-feeding.

When this medicine is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Rarely, mild gastrointestinal disturbance and the like may occur at the start of treatment.

summaryTable.What it is for: Adjunctive treatment of asthenia (functional weakness)

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Tablet (E24700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D, vitamin B1 and vitamin B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age; for poor development of the bones and teeth and the prevention of rickets; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for beriberi and eye fatigue; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 8 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, once a day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; if you have had kidney stones; if you are being given cardiac glycosides; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If there is no improvement in symptoms after 1 month or more of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, loose stools, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, fluid on the lungs, loss of appetite, redness of the skin, hives, eczema, rash, a maculopapular rash, itching, swelling, or fluid retention (in people with kidney failure or heart failure) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, B1 and B6 and of zinc; bone and tooth development and prevention of rickets; neuralgia and muscle/joint pain; beriberi; eye fatigue

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Tablet (D65400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for melasma.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, 2 times a day, after meals. Do not take it continuously for more than 2 months.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is under 15 years of age; if you are taking an oral medicine that contains tranexamic acid; if you are being given thrombin; if you have severe kidney impairment or hepatic coma; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; or if you have thrombosis (cerebral thrombosis, myocardial infarction, thrombophlebitis, pulmonary embolism and the like).

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you are aged 55 years or over; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are at risk of thrombosis; if you have kidney impairment; if you have cystinuria; if it is hard to tell whether a mark on your skin is melasma; or if the melasma is dark, uneven in tone or raised above the surface of the skin.

If you stop taking this medicine and the melasma comes back so that you take it again, leave a gap of at least 2 months, and again do not take it for more than 2 months. This medicine may affect urine and stool test results.

Do not take this medicine while you are taking tranexamic acid or thrombin. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking medicines that may cause thrombosis, such as oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy.

This medicine makes blood clots harder to dissolve, so watch for early signs of thrombosis (severe headache, slurred speech, a crushing chest pain lasting more than 10 minutes, sudden shortness of breath, pain or swelling in one calf, sudden difficulty breathing of unknown cause, or a temporary loss of consciousness with chest pain). If rash, itching, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, heartburn, palpitations, headache or light-headedness appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (B00200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for hives, eczema and itching.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Ages 8 to 14 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age or an older person; if you are debilitated; if you have an allergic constitution, high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, swelling, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not use this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), other oral medicines for rhinitis, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (cold medicines, antitussives and expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or preparations containing diphenhydramine (including preparations applied to the skin). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide). Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If hives, swelling and chest tightness appear immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing; if the amount of urine decreases, the face and limbs swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises or headache appears; or if myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis), rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite or difficulty passing urine appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E07000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency; to supply vitamin E and vitamin B1 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age; to relieve the symptoms of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of the menopause such as stiff shoulders and neck, numb hands and feet and cold hands and feet; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, once a day, or 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil or have had a reaction to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soy or peanuts; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have severe kidney failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment, low blood protein or diabetes; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism (hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia, pancreatitis and the like), or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; or if you are at particular risk from fat overload.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness of the skin, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss or restlessness appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E81700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain (stiff shoulders), bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, period pain and pain from injury, and to reduce fever when there are chills (feeling cold and shivery) and a temperature.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 capsules at a time, 1 to 3 times a day. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 3 times a day. Avoid taking the dose on an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause bleeding in the digestive tract.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease should avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day). Patients with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) should consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine if high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) is needed.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have hypersensitivity or allergy to soybean oil; if you have hypersensitivity to soy or peanuts; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if the user is an older person; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot absorb fluid; if you are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to them.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with other antipyretic analgesics, cold medicines, sedatives or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with diuretics, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants or steroids. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, bleeding in the digestive tract, stomach discomfort, dizziness or swelling appears, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes) or asthma appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, low back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulders, bruise, fracture and sprain pain, period pain, injury pain, fever

groups.title: Soft capsule (E65000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms from a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness (congested and reddened skin) and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), asthma, impaired liver function (general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) and the like) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soy or peanuts; if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood potassium; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which abnormal iron metabolism causes iron to be deposited in the liver and pancreas), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; if you have kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; if you have alkalosis or gout; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; if you have had kidney stones; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

While taking this medicine, do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful swollen joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness of the skin, loose stools, hives, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, high blood potassium, wind, stomach pain, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid on the lungs appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a tonic and for nutritional supply in a weak constitution, physical fatigue, during or after illness, loss of appetite, nutritional disorders, febrile and wasting illnesses, and pregnancy and breast-feeding.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 1 bottle at a time, once a day, after a meal. Use this medicine by mouth only; it must not be used for injection.
groups.caution:
Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or have had an allergic reaction.

This medicine contains herbal extracts, so a sediment sometimes forms. This does not change how well it works, so shake it well before taking it. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

If nausea, vomiting or loose stools appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
